'''David Ginzburg''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: דוד גינזבורג) is a professor of mathematics at [[Tel Aviv University]] working in [[number theory]] and [[automorphic forms]].

==Career==
Ginzburg received his PhD in mathematics from Tel Aviv University in 1988 under the supervision of [[Stephen Gelbart]].<ref name="mathgenealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=32529}}</ref> He is a professor of mathematics at Tel Aviv University.<ref name="Homepage">{{cite web|url=https://english.tau.ac.il/profile/ginzburg |publisher=[[Tel Aviv University]] |title=Prof. David Ginzburg |access-date=29 February 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
Together with [[Stephen Rallis]] and [[David Soudry]], Ginzburg wrote a series of papers about automorphic descent culminating in their book "The descent map from automorphic representations of GL(''n'') to classical groups". Their automorphic descent method constructs an explicit inverse map to the (standard) [[Langlands program#Functoriality|Langlands functorial lift]] and has had major applications to the analysis of functoriality.<ref>J. Cogdell, H. Jacquet, D. Jiang, S. Kudla, (2015), eds. "Steve Rallis (1942–2012)," ''Journal of Number Theory'', 146, 1–3</ref>  Also, using the "Rallis tower property" from Rallis's 1984 paper on the [[Howe duality conjecture]], they studied global exceptional correspondences and found new examples of functorial lifts.<ref>W.T. Gan, Y. Qiu, and S. Takeda (2014) "The Regularized Siegel–Weil Formula (The Second Term Identity) and the Rallis Inner Product Formula," Inventiones Math. 198, 739–831</ref>
